card.title: Your Risk, My Cost
card.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

transfer.action: I lay my repair bill beside the risky choice about {prop}.
transfer.opening: Your gamble keeps arriving on my account. {request}
transfer.response: I want a vote in consequences I pay for. {counter}
transfer.closing: Then find a way for the invoice to recognize your independence.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Cancel your camping contest so my lawn doesn't pay for thirty tents. Show me you're on my side.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'd lose the entry fee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Yes. That's one consequence finally landing beside the decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Isn't that a harsh loyalty test?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then offer a real sacrifice that doesn't grow back in my garden.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses S208-single-b's thirty campers and lawn-maintenance consequences, adapting D203-single-a's costly proof of being on A's side to cancellation of a camping contest. A1 demands cancellation; A3 uses B2's lost entry fee as a cost attached to B's choice, and A5 answers B4's objection by inviting another real sacrifice. The contest and entry fee originate in this pair, not the single seeds. Pair semantic review remains pending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give up your first turn teaching the dog to fetch glasses. I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Training matters to me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let protecting my budget matter enough to cost you a turn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I said I'd clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm asking for loyalty before the breakage, not help sweeping my share afterwards.

bespokePairs.seedUse: Uses S208-single-a's dog, glasses, replacement costs and inadequate cleanup offer with D203-single-a's surrendered first turn as a costly loyalty gesture. A1 asks for that turn; A3 answers B2 by making protection of A's budget worth a sacrifice, and A5 uses B4's cleanup offer to insist on loyalty before breakage. This fixes the crossed exact references; pair semantic review remains pending.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you teach the dog to fetch glasses, can I vote? I buy the glasses.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's my training experiment.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And my experiment is making rent after the breakages.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll clean up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Include replacing the glasses in your definition of clean.

card.title: Lose Something for Me
card.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Will you give me your first turn, even if it costs you the match?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why would I do that?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You said you were on my side. This side has a cost.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I meant emotionally.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then lend the emotion a turn so I can see it.

card.title: Your Risk, My Cost
card.instruction: Treat every choice around you as a risk whose consequences may land on you. Press for a voice in decisions you cannot control.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're inviting thirty people to camp in our garden? I maintain the lawn.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's only one weekend.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Grass experiences time differently. I want a say in tent placement.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're making this complicated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm trying to keep your simple weekend out of my next six Saturdays.

card.title: Lose Something for Me
card.instruction: Create a loyalty test by asking them to accept a real disadvantage on your behalf.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Miss the prize ceremony and come to my tiny opening night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm receiving the prize.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I know. Coming wouldn't mean much if you had nothing else to do.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's an unfair test.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Maybe. I'm trying to discover whether I'm more than the convenient option.

beats.text: Thirty people camping in our garden? I maintain that lawn.

beats.speaker: B
